speaker: Doctor
text: The blood and sedimentation results are normal, which makes a typical bacterial cellulitis less likely. Can you tell me if the lesion is associated with a recent insect bite or trauma, and does it have a visible central crater?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of Crohn's disease and diabetes, combined with a lesion that started after an ant bite and has grown over a month, this raises concern for an atypical infection or cutaneous malignancy rather than simple cellulitis. Has the lesion developed any raised, rolled borders, and do you notice a central area of depression or ulceration?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Painful ulcerative lesion on the right leg. I also have Lesion has a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders, History of ant bite at the site of the lesion, Pitting pedal edema of the lower extremities, Dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cutaneous Leishmaniasis

The description of a painful ulcer with a central necrotic base, purplish irregular borders, and a history of an ant bite is highly suggestive of Cutaneous Leishmaniasis. I have already noted your history of Crohn's and diabetes, which increases the risk of atypical presentations. Please confirm if you have any history of travel to endemic regions, such as parts of the Mediterranean, the Middle East, or South America, or if you have been exposed to sandflies.
